newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 14.5/15.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 14.5/15.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 14.5/15.0 percent on Thursday morning after the central bank raised its overnight bilateral rate to 14.0 percent.

Dealers said the central bank move to raise overnight rates by one percentage point and the absence of short-term securities (SBPUs) purchases by Bank Indonesia helped drain excess supply of short-term liquidity.
Dealers said the central bank will not buy any SBPUs on Thursday.
"It's a smart move from the central bank to contain short-term liquidity without shocking the market. This will help prevent dollar buying with cheap rupiah," one Japanese bank dealer said.
The central bank raised its interest rates for overnight bilateral papers by one percentage point on Thursday while keeping other rates unchanged.

The bank offered overnight SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at eight percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Dealers said the move pushed short-dated swaps up, with overnight swap rising to 0.30/0.35 from -0.2/par and tom/next to 0.4/0.5 from -0.7 points.
Longer-term rates were higher following expensive swaps.
One-month money was at 15.0/15.5, two at 15.25/15.50 and three at 15.5/16.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 14.34 percent, compared with 13.97 percent on Tuesday.
